newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki still edgy, soft, PK Cables shines.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki still edgy, soft, PK Cables shines.

text.p: Shares fell on Thursday after Wall Street's losses overnight and as Swedish-led attempts at higher ground failed amid nervous sentiment, brokers said.
The HEX index ended off 0.21 percent at 2,738.93 with volume 520 million markka, 35 percent of it in bourse engine Nokia which tracked Swedish rival Ericsson higher to close up 3.50 at 287.00 markka.
Forestries rose on recent dollar strengthening against the markka, although the greenback opened weak in the U.S.
Trade was modest with many players sidelined ahead of key U.S. jobs data on Friday which could give a new signal on the likelihood of any further hike in U.S. interest rates, brokers said.

Newcomer to the list, electronic wiring and components cablemaker PK Cables, shined on its first day of trade, closing at 70 markka, 13 percent above its 62.00 markka open and 52 percent above the 46 markka share issue.
"It's surprisingly strong. That was a good share issue," one broker said.
Pharmaceuticals group Orion eased in fair volume after sharp gains on Wednesday, down 4.00 markka at 195.00.
But brokers said all eyes were really on U.S. payroll data for a clue on whether the Federal reserve may opt to raise its federal funds rate again after hiking it on March 25.

"Tomorrow's U.S. employment figures will determine the direction," one broker said. "In our view the markets have already discounted another rate hike, so there's room to move up (in prices)," one analyst said.

The U.S. March unemployent rate -- due to be released at 1330 GMT -- is forecast at 5.2 percent on average, compared to 5.3 percent reported in February, and average hourly earnings are forecast up 0.4 percent compared to 0.2 percent in February.
